conviction_note: Ethos has guided far below what it then printed twice running (Q2 guide $114-118m, printed $189.6m; FY guide raised from $561-565m to $727-731m), and sell-side Q3 revenue consensus ($163-168m) sits barely above the $160-164m guide. So a large reported beat is the base case. But the stock is +46% since the last print and +18.9% in 20 days, sits 2.8% off its 52-week high, took a JPM valuation downgrade, and saw short interest triple into the print. The whisper is well above consensus and much of the beat is priced. Hence p_up 57 on a 24% absolute move (scaled +3.4), against a findings sum of +1.0. The findings sum is smaller because the run-up finding nets out most of the guide-conservatism finding, while p_up carries the lean the beat-and-raise reaction history (+32%, +21%) gives.
bar: Q3 2026 revenue: company guide $160-164m and adj. EBITDA $23-25m, from the Q2 release (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001788451/000119312526330556/life-ex99_1.htm, 2026-08-03). Sell-side revenue consensus is $163.3m-$168.1m across two Benzinga snapshots (https://www.benzinga.com/quote/LIFE/earnings-forecasts). EPS consensus is disputed ($0.30 Benzinga vs $0.09 Earnings Whispers), so EPS is not used as the bar. The bar is sourced to the company guide; the buy-side whisper is unsourced but implied well above consensus by the run-up.
positioning_check: Short interest 4,113,640 shares at the 2026-10-15 settlement, 2.87 days to cover, up from 3,710,794 (09-30), 1,819,799 (09-15) and 1,259,754 (08-31) (https://equibles.com/stocks/life/shortinterest). That is about 13% of the 31.55m Class A shares outstanding at 2026-07-27 (Q2 10-Q cover) and about 6.5% of all shares. Skew_25d is +5.37 vol points (modest downside paid). Put/call open interest ratio is 0.02, so the open interest is overwhelmingly calls. Event-implied move is 23.79%. The shorts building into a rising stock are squeeze fuel on a beat, and the call-heavy open interest says longs are positioned for upside.

findings.finding: Ethos guides far below its outcomes. The Q2 2026 revenue guide of $114-118m (given 2026-05-06) printed at $189.6m, +63% over the midpoint, and the FY2026 guide was raised from $561-565m to $727-731m. Q3 is now guided at $160-164m, which implies a 15% sequential drop from Q2's $189.6m, while sell-side consensus sits at only $163-168m. A print near the Q1/Q2 run-rate (~$190m) would be ~+13% over consensus.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Both prior large revenue beats against this company's own guide were bought hard: Q1 2026 (2026-05-06) +32.31%, Q2 2026 (2026-08-03) +21.11% close-to-close (baseline). The first print (2026-02-25), a small beat, moved +3.72%.
findings.why_not_priced: Sell-side consensus ($163-168m) is anchored within a few million of the guide despite two quarters of 60%+ beats. If the market priced the pattern fully, consensus would be near $190m and the stock would not need the beat to hold its 46% post-print run. It is partly priced: the run-up says the buy-side whisper is above consensus.
findings.independence: Q2 release on EDGAR (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001788451/000119312526330556/life-ex99_1.htm) gives Q2 $189.6m and the Q3 guide. Q1 release gives Q1 $193.1m (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001788451/000119312526208936/life-ex99_1.htm). Benzinga carries the prior FY guide of $561-565m. These sources share the company's own numbers.

findings.finding: The FY2026 guide of $727-731m less H1 actuals ($382.7m) and the Q3 midpoint ($162m) implies Q4 of only ~$184m, below the Q1/Q2 run-rate of ~$191m. Any Q3 beat therefore mechanically lifts the FY range, as happened in August (+$166m raise on a $74m Q2 beat).
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The August FY raise from $561-565m to $727-731m came with the +21.11% reaction. The May release, which carried the first FY guide, moved +32.31%.
findings.why_not_priced: Consensus that tracks the Q3 guide implies the sell-side also models Q4 near the implied ~$184m. A visible FY raise is the line the stock traded on in August.
findings.independence: Shares the company-guide document with the first finding, and the raise is largely a mechanical consequence of a Q3 beat, so it is sized down for the overlap. The H1 revenue of $382.7m is from the Q2 10-Q (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001788451/000119312526335209/life-20260630.htm).

findings.finding: The bar has been raised by the tape. The stock is +18.9% in 20 days, about +46% since the 2026-08-03 print, 2.8% below its 52-week high and +336% off its low. JPMorgan downgraded it to Neutral on valuation (~2026-10-01, $37 PT, stock then $33.57), and it has rallied ~28% since. The 9-analyst average PT of $37.50 sits ~13% below spot.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No prior LIFE print came into a run-up this large. Into Q2 the stock had not rallied 46% from the previous print.
findings.why_not_priced: It is the price itself. It is filed because it sets the effective bar: a beat merely to ~$185m against a whisper near $190-200m can be sold. The skew (+5.37) agrees with this direction.
findings.independence: Baseline tape: run_up_20d +18.93%, pct_from_52w_high -2.83%. The JPM downgrade is reported in German-language coverage (https://goldesel.de/aktien/news/atyr-pharma-aktie-jpmorgan-einstufung-betrifft-nicht-das-biotechunternehmen). Earnings Whispers gives the +45.8% drift since the last release (https://beta.earningswhispers.com/go/w/LIFE).

findings.finding: Short interest more than tripled into the print, from 1.26m shares (2026-08-31) to 4.11m (2026-10-15, 2.87 days to cover). That is ~13% of the 31.55m Class A shares, against put/call open interest of only 0.02, so a beat meets a growing short base.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Short interest was ~1.7-1.9m into the Q2 print (07-15/07-31 settlements), which moved +21.11%.
findings.why_not_priced: FINRA publishes with a lag and the 10-30 settlement is not yet out. A squeeze would show as calls bid and a shrinking short base before the print, and neither is visible. The rising shorts may also be informed bears (the Bear Cave/Hunterbrook thesis), which is why the size is modest.
findings.independence: The 2026-09-30 figure of 3.71m shares and 2.0 days to cover is corroborated on massive.com (https://massive.com/quote/life). The Class A share count is from the Q2 10-Q cover.

findings.finding: Margins are guided down sharply. Q3 adj. EBITDA guide is $23-25m (~15% margin at the midpoint) against Q2's $35.2m (19%). Management attributes this to a third-party mix with 'skinnier' unit economics and to 'strategic growth investments'. ARPU fell 8% y/y to $1,758 on a whole-life mix shift, and ad spend more than doubled y/y.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The Q2 release already carried margin compression (third-party +90%, ARPU -8%) and still moved +21.11%. This holder base has looked through mix-driven margin before.
findings.why_not_priced: The guided margin is known. What is not priced is whether the Q3 beat comes with EBITDA beating proportionally or with spend absorbing it. A beat on revenue with EBITDA inside $23-25m would read as low quality.
findings.independence: The Q2 release carries the EBITDA guide (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001788451/000119312526330556/life-ex99_1.htm). Insider Monkey's 'margins quietly compress' piece (https://www.insidermonkey.com/blog/ethos-life-grows-revenue-113-while-margins-quietly-compress-1826884/?amp=1) makes the same point.

findings.finding: The CFO said Q2 operating cash flow ($35.7m) included an $8m timing benefit from a settlement with a carrier partner that is expected to reverse in Q3, so Q3 operating cash flow will be optically weaker.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: None on record for cash-flow items on this name.
findings.why_not_priced: It was disclosed on the call, so it is largely priced. It is cash timing only, with no path to revenue or the guide.
findings.independence: Shares the call transcript with the margin finding. A Nasdaq call-highlights summary repeats it (https://www.nasdaq.com/articles/ethos-technologies-inc-class-common-stock-q2-earnings-call-highlights).

findings.finding: On 2026-10-28 Ethos and Liberty Mutual expanded their April white-label relationship. Liberty Mutual's Ethos-powered life product is now sold through its call centers as well as online, with bundled auto/home savings for Ethos policyholders. This supports third-party channel growth (+90% y/y in Q2), mostly from Q4 onward.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No measured reaction to carrier announcements. The April 2026 Liberty Mutual launch came before the stock's run from ~$14.
findings.why_not_priced: It was announced five days before the print, so it is mostly priced. It may surface as a Q4/2027 commentary driver on the call.
findings.independence: The release is syndicated on easternherald (https://easternherald.com/press-release/ethos-and-liberty-mutual-expand-relationship-to-help-protect-who-and-what-matters-most/), the same source.

findings.finding: The CEO (Peter Colis) and the President (Lingke Wang) sold shares on 2026-10-14 to 10-16 at ~$37.64-39.58 after converting derivative securities, under Rule 10b5-1 plans.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Post-lock-up insider and VC selling (July 28-29, GV 2019 GP) preceded the +21% Q2 reaction.
findings.why_not_priced: These are public Form 4s on pre-scheduled plans, so they are largely priced and carry little information.
findings.independence: A second Form 4 (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001788451/000208926326000018/form4-10162026_051003.xml) covers the same window.

findings.finding: Revenue rests on persistency estimates. In Q1 2026 Ethos took a $16.5m non-cash charge because early persistency on third-party policies (2H24-2025) was better than projected, which raised agent compensation. The persistency reserve liability (cash received above revenue recognized) rose from $4.9m at 2025 year-end to $43.2m at 2026-06-30, a conservative cushion. The direction of any Q3 true-up is unknown.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The Q1 print carried the $16.5m charge and still moved +32.31%.
findings.why_not_priced: The reserve build sits in a 10-Q glossary and balance sheet and is not in previews. Better persistency is a revenue tailwind under variable-consideration accounting, but it has also produced expense true-ups, so the sign is ambiguous and the size is small.
findings.independence: The Q2 10-Q gives the reserve balance (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001788451/000119312526335209/life-20260630.htm). The S-1/A gives the variable-consideration policy.

findings.finding: Short-seller and legal overhang. The Bear Cave (Hunterbrook Media) published 'Problems at Ethos' on 2026-05-21, alleging a lead-gen business with a narrow moat, consumer complaints to state regulators and upfront recognition of renewal commissions. An SBS Law 'fraud investigation' solicitation followed on 2026-11-01, a day before the print.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The stock fell after the May 21 report, then rose ~150% through two beats.
findings.why_not_priced: It is old and public. The SBS solicitation is boilerplate with no new allegation found. It matters only if the release or call addresses accounting.
findings.independence: stockanalysis.com news feed lists the SBS Law notice dated Nov 1 (https://stockanalysis.com/stocks/LIFE).

findings.finding: Carrier concentration is high. Carrier A and Carrier B were 43% and 36% of Q2 revenue, and three carriers held 67%/13%/12% of receivables at 2026-06-30, so one carrier's pricing or appetite change moves the quarter.
findings.why_not_priced: It is a disclosed structural risk. No sign of a carrier change was found.
findings.independence: The Q2 10-Q on EDGAR is the same document.

outside_window.finding: LIMRA's Q3 2026 US individual life sales survey (Q2: term premium +6-7%, policy count +8%) usually publishes mid-November, after the window. It cannot be seen by the exit.

CEO remarks at Goldman Communacopia (2026-09-09): no transcript content found

rejected_candidates.detail: The disputed EPS bar is folded into the 'bar' field. Sizing uses the revenue and EBITDA guide instead

baseline_tension: The fundamental read (another large beat against a deliberately low guide) agrees with the call-heavy open interest and rising shorts as squeeze fuel. It cuts against the +18.9% 20-day run-up, the 46% post-print rally and the modest put skew (+5.37), which say much of the beat is in the price. That pulls p_up to 57 rather than the 65+ the guide pattern alone would justify.
lessons_applied: Two readings of one document are one finding: the FY-raise guidance finding shares the company-guide document with the Q3 beat finding and follows mechanically from it, so it was cut from +2.0 to +1.5 for the overlap
Verify the bar: the bar is sourced to the company guide plus two Benzinga consensus snapshots ($163-168m), so findings were not capped. The disputed EPS consensus is not used

A verified fact is not a predicted reaction: checked the reaction history. This name has bought both large beats (+32%, +21%), so the beat finding was not damped further. The run-up finding already carries the priced-in risk
Positioning: looked up short interest before the negatives (13% of Class A, 2.9 days to cover, tripling). The only sizable negative (run-up) agrees with the skew, so it was left unchanged
Sweep flagged baseline_history_trustworthy false: the three prior moves are 8-K 2.02-timed company prints (Feb 25, May 6, Aug 3), so the history was kept as the scale
